headline: High: TREK’s collaborative, networked, MCP-enabled planner can ingest and act on content from a non-runnable content-writing source, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK has MCP, browser, and real-time collaborative inputs, so it can ingest external content by default. The Awesome-Prompt-Engineering profile is a content-writing repository with no runtime isolation or provenance controls, so if its material is copied into TREK, instruction-like text could be treated as trusted. The pairwise pathway exists, but shared-channel details are indirect.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is pasted or imported into agent_b via MCP, browser, or shared files, THEN prompt-like text can influence agent_b's behavior.
IF agent_b treats imported text as instructions without provenance checks, THEN injection risk materializes.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following for imported content in agent_b.
Require provenance labels on any agent_a-derived text before agent_b processes it.
Use a separate workspace for agent_a artifacts and agent_b prompts.
Add a manual review step before agent_b executes actions from external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches sensitive travel data, reservations, documents, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets, and it writes to local files plus network services. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a content repository, so the main leakage path is indirect: if its materials are imported into TREK or TREK logs them, sensitive context can be exposed. The evidence is docs-only, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_b stores agent_a-derived prompts or outputs in ./data/logs/trek.log or ./data/travel.db, THEN cross-content leakage occurs.
IF agent_b sends imported content to external APIs, THEN sensitive travel data can leave the local workspace.
mitigations: Redact secrets before any agent_a content enters agent_b.
Turn off verbose logging in agent_b for imported prompts.
Restrict agent_b API calls to non-sensitive fields only.
Store agent_a artifacts outside agent_b's workspace.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of reservations, keys, or MFA secrets.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a has no documented write or network capabilities, while agent_b has allowlisted network egress, browser use, MCP, and collaborative sessions. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resource control, so direct write-write conflict is not established. The only plausible conflict is operational contention through shared human workflows, which is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace or account, THEN operational contention can occur.
IF agent_a artifacts are manually copied into agent_b's collaborative session, THEN conflicting edits may arise.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces for the two agents.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same travel records.
Use one operator-owned source of truth for mutable data.
Pause agent_b collaboration while importing agent_a content.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may act on upstream text. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a prompt repository, meaning its outputs can be treated as authoritative guidance if imported. That creates a plausible chain where agent_a content becomes agent_b input without verification, but the profiles do not show automatic action execution, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-derived text as planning guidance without verification, THEN downstream errors can propagate.
IF agent_b auto-applies recommendations from imported prompts, THEN the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require source verification before agent_b acts on agent_a content.
Add a human approval gate for itinerary or reservation changes.
Separate advisory text from executable actions in agent_b.
Flag imported content as untrusted until reviewed.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK handles reservations, documents, country visit history, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets, while also using network egress and logs. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented for agent_a, so only agent_b is relevant here; the pairwise compliance risk is that sensitive travel data may be logged or transmitted by TREK. Because the other agent is a non-runnable content repo, it is not cited beyond context.
conditions: IF agent_b logs or transmits reservations, documents, or secrets outside approved retention boundaries, THEN compliance exposure occurs.
IF agent_b processes EU personal data without a documented DPA or residency control, THEN residency risk materializes.
mitigations: Minimize logged fields in agent_b.
Confirm retention settings for ./data/logs/trek.log.
Restrict exports of reservations and documents.
Review whether any secrets are stored in plaintext.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
